messages:
morgan: Heads-up — we saw OTLP exporter throttling yesterday during the batch job window and a bunch of traces fell through into cold storage. Can we discuss TTL by environment before I push the quick fix?

clara: ugh. saw the S3 bill jump. how big was the backfill? any idea which services were noisy? :grimacing:

morgan: Rough numbers: ~1.2M spans re-ingested, ~120GB additional cold objects, ~3k cold reads triggered for rehydrate queries. Most traffic from feature/experiment services in staging + a burst from recommendations in prod.

javier: For context, our current config is uniform: hot_ttl=14d, cold_ttl=365d, promotion_on_query=true. That uniformity is what made the staging burst costly.

samir: Proposal: split TTLs by env and by importance bucket. e.g. staging: hot=3d, cold=30d; prod-default: hot=30d, cold=365d; prod-critical: hot=90d, cold=730d.

elena: +1 for env split. But need to add quota + rehydration guardrails on console so users understand cost. We had a bunch of ad-hoc queries that rehydrated large traces.

clara: Agree. Also need per-service budget enforcement. Maybe map a quota to service tags in spans? We can gate rehydrate if estimated bytes > X unless owner ack.

morgan: Two implementation options: 1) exporter-side tags -> mark low-priority spans as SAMPLE_LOW and route to cold-only early (no hot cache). 2) routing-layer TTL override by env/service at ingest. Which is lower-risk?

javier: #2 is simpler to rollout (central config change) but risks immediate effect across many tenants. #1 requires SDK changes and changes to ingestion parser.

samir: Could do phased approach: first enforce env-based TTL (staging low), add console toggle to preview impact and canary for 10% of prod teams. Then implement SAMPLE_LOW path in SDKs for long-term.

elena: UX note: console should show estimated cost delta for TTL change before you apply it. e.g. "Reducing hot TTL from 30d->7d saves ~X tokens/month but increases rehydrate ops by Y". Otherwise PMs will push back.

clara: Ops ask: how do we measure rehydrate latency impact? We need to ensure query SLOs and maybe surface a fallback: if rehydrate > 2s then return partial and queue rehydrate async.

morgan: Good point. We can also add a soft-fallback policy (fast-path: try hot+cache, if miss and trace > threshold return marker pointing to "cold_pending" and optionally enqueue warm-up).

javier: Implementation checklist I propose: 
- config layer: TTL_by_env + TTL_by_service (config store + rollout)
- console: preview cost impact + per-service override toggle
- telemetry: metrics for cold_reads, rehydrate_latencies, estimated_rehydrate_bytes
- rollout: canary 10% prod teams -> 50% -> all

samir: Also add exporter tagging RFC so teams can mark low-fidelity spans (sampling reasons). That'll reduce hot traffic for noisy services.

elena: Compliance note: some customers need >365d cold retention. We must support per-tenant overrides via enterprise contract, not console default.

morgan: Agree. I'll draft a short RFC with the phased approach and timeline. Can someone volunteer to own the console preview card?

clara: I can pick up console preview MVP (estimate 3-4 days). Will need cost model inputs from finance.

javier: I'll own config rollout and canary orchestration.

samir: I'll start working on exporter tagging RFC and a small PoC in the ingest path.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: New canary config created: ttl-env-overrides/v1 -> canary namespace (10% prod). No deploys yet.

morgan: Thanks all. I'll circulate RFC by EOD and add PR for staging TTL change (staging: hot=3d, cold=30d) — staging change will be non-canary and reversible.

clara: Cool. Once staging is live we'll monitor cold_reads and cost delta and decide next steps. :thumbsup:
